# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 96)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; **late April: gusty raw day with rain whipping pavement, end of day with early light, smoke flat over fields; church service with rattling rain on windows; autumn of third year (river crossing at Quenwick)**

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist; talented mimic
- **Status**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church; living with Rawdon in Brompton lodgings; marriage revealed through letter on pincushion
- **Current Position**: Denied access to Miss Crawley at Park Lane; letters unopened; encountered and cut pitilessly by Miss Crawley at Fenmere while driving with Rawdon

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca; living with her in Brompton lodgings
- **Current Status**: Cut by Miss Crawley at Fenmere encounter; sank back in carriage with oath; drove desperately homewards

**Miss Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon
- **Response to Marriage**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute's nursing; letters unopened; not recovering from shock
- **Medical Status**: Mr. Clump and Dr. Squills recommend confinement counterproductive; advise change, fresh air, gaiety, little drives as remedies
- **Recent Encounters**: Cut Rebecca and Rawdon pitilessly at Fenmere

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; positioned as nurse; continuously present at Park Lane; cultivates staff loyalty; takes Miss Crawley on diversionary drives; tells stories against Rawdon and Rebecca

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married to George Osborne; ceremony performed late April in chapel near Fulham Road; dressed in brown silk pelisse, straw bonnet with pink ribbon, white Chantilly lace veil (gift from Jos), gold chain and watch (gift from Captain Dobbin), mother's diamond brooch
- **Marriage Service**: Her response came "fluttering up to her lips from her heart, scarcely heard by anybody except Captain Dobbin"; George's "I will" sounded in deep bass; rain rattled down on windows during service; Mrs. Sedley wept throughout; parson's tones echoed sadly through empty chapel walls
- **Emotional State at Marriage**: Fear overcome by love; George's look of gloom gone, seemed quite proud and radiant
- **Living Situation**: At St. Adelaide Villas with reduced circumstances (before marriage)

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards; over head and ears in debt; gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married Amelia Osborne in late April; pale and agitated before ceremony; wiped face with large scented yellow bandanna handkerchief; swallowed couple glasses of curacao nervously; servant packed his desk and dressing-case into waiting coach; wore blue coat and brass buttons with neat buff waistcoat
- **Military Status**: Captain; mobilized for campaign; regiment expecting orders for foreign service to hunt down Napoleon
- **Father's Pressure - OVERCOME**: John Osborne demanded George marry Miss Swartz (heiress); George obstinately refused; temporized citing imminent foreign service; demonstrated coolness and defiance in dinner confrontation making father quail; relationship severed for "some days" after encounter; secured "stock of provisions" on day of first confrontation; old Osborne expected him at Russell Square daily but George never came; George and Dobbin left town
- **Pre-Marriage State**: Married despite father's opposition and financial threats; his pallor and nervousness attributed to first marriage experience; slept little night before ceremony; agitated in morning
- **At Ceremony**: Looked quite proud and radiant after service completed; told Jos "It's your turn, William" regarding Dobbin; spoke fondly to Dobbin putting hand on his shoulder; drove away with bride in carriage through rain; told small damp urchins to "Get out of the way, you little devils"

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed with marriage; urged George necessity of immediate action before regiment's orders
- **Marriage Gifts**: Presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; stepped up as groomsman to George
- **Emotional State at Ceremony**: Touched Amelia on cheek after service; later left chapel in reverie; rejected Jos Sedley's invitation to tiffin, having no heart to feast; put weeping Mrs. Sedley and attendants into carriage with Jos without further words; left chapel solitary
- **Character**: Soft-hearted, melted by women's pain; extraordinarily eager in marriage conduct; convinced George and Emmy should not be barked of happiness by want of means
- **Military Status**: Forms portion of British army mobilized; in blue coat and brass buttons at Slaughters' Coffee-house; abandoned military frock and French-grey trousers

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Strategy Change - FAILED**: Demanded George marry Miss Swartz (heiress); based demand on City information; offered incentives (five thousand pounds, ten thousand a year income); demanded daily dinners with heiress
- **Father-Son Confrontation**: George showed resolution and defiance making father quail; tussle ensuing; George left town shortly after, never returning to Russell Square despite old Osborne's anxious daily expectation
- **Expectations Re: Supplies**: Old Osborne felt "pretty easy about his adversary," confidently expected George's unconditional submission when supplies fell short; thought relief was temporary; waited for operation of "screw"; told sisters of dispute but ordered them to welcome George on return as if nothing happened; George's cover laid daily but he never came
- **Outcome**: George married Amelia despite father's opposition; financial rupture appears imminent ("must take his pack and walk out of house" threat made but not yet executed)

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Ruined merchant; declared bankrupt; initially forbade match with Osborne but softened after Dobbin's intervention
- **At Marriage Ceremony**: Did not attend; Jos acted as father giving away bride

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; proved faithful consoler; accepted reduced circumstances
- **At Marriage Ceremony**: Sat in pew and whimpered greatly throughout service; consoled by Irish maid-servant and Mrs. Clapp from lodgings; gave Amelia her diamond brooch (almost only trinket left to her); took hysterical adieu of daughter after service; was placed in carriage with Jos Sedley by Dobbin

**Jos Sedley** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's brother; splendid appearance at marriage ceremony
- **At Marriage Ceremony**: Fatter than ever with higher shirt collars, redder face, shirt-frill flaunting gorgeously from variegated waistcoat; wore Hessians that shone brilliantly, light green coat with fine white wedding favour like magnolia; gave away bride as father's representative; kissed sister for first time in many months; invited Dobbin to tiffin after ceremony; traveled home in carriage with weeping Mrs. Sedley and attendants

**Miss Swartz** [CHARACTER]
- Young heiress; wealthy; possesses estates in St. Kitt's; ten thousand a year income; simple, good-natured, adorns person with skill
- **Status Re: George**: Encouraged by John Osborne and George's sisters as suitable match; George found union with her "doubly ludicrous and odious"; referred to her as "mahogany charmer"; horrified at idea of being seen with her in carriages and opera-boxes; George defended Amelia passionately against her, wrung her hand in earnest; George married Amelia instead, rejecting all pressure to wed Miss Swartz

**Other Characters**
- **Major Wagstaff of the Engineers**: Friend of Dobbin; joked with him about his splendid costume and agitation at Slaughters' Coffee-house; Dobbin promised to send him cake when married
- **Comrades at Slaughters' Coffee-house**: Gentlemen who joked Dobbin about his costume, asked if he was going to be married
- **John (Waiter at Slaughters')**: Served George curacao at coffee-house
- **George's Servant**: Packed master's desk and dressing-case; traveled with George and Dobbin in coach; cursed rain and dampness; mentioned finding better trap at church-door
- **Coachman**: Steaming beside valet in rain
- **Irish Maid-servant**: Consoled Mrs. Sedley during ceremony
- **Mrs. Clapp from Lodgings**: Consoled Mrs. Sedley during ceremony
- **Parson**: Officiated at marriage service; tones echoed sadly through empty chapel walls

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED**: Married in chapel near Fulham Road, late April; small party only (Jos as bride's representative, Dobbin as groomsman, Mrs. Sedley, servants); George pale and agitated before ceremony; appeared proud and radiant after; bride dressed elegantly in brown silk pelisse, straw bonnet, white Chantilly lace veil; rain during service; minimal witnesses
- **DOBBIN'S SACRIFICIAL ROLE**: Gift of gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman to George; afterward left ceremony in reverie, rejecting celebration, departed without further words—emotional toll evident
- **JOHN OSBORNE'S DEFEAT**: Demanded George marry Miss Swartz; George refused obstinately; severed communication for "some days"; secured supplies; left town with Dobbin; old Osborne waited anxiously at Russell Square but George never returned; marriage proceeded despite father's opposition and financial threats
- **MILITARY IMPERATIVE FULFILLED**: Marriage completed before expected marching orders; regiment mobilized for foreign service to hunt down Napoleon; George and Dobbin in uniform at coffee-house preparation
- **FINANCIAL RUPTURE IMMINENT**: George married without father's consent or blessing; old Osborne threatened "take his pack and walk out of house" if George refused Miss Swartz or flung away eight thousand a year income; status of paternal support now uncertain but marriage proceeded regardless
- **MISS SWARTZ REJECTED**: Despite John Osborne's incentives and pressure, George married Amelia; heiress not secured; ten thousand a year income rejected; marriage considered "ludicrous and odious" alternative avoided
